t: 2791. Count Paths That Can Form a Palindrome in a Tree
o: Each node v (except root) has a character on its edge to its parent. For a pair (u,v), collect the multiset of characters on the path u↔v; it can be rearranged into a palindrome iff at most one character has odd count. Path characters combine as XOR of root-path masks: mask(v) = mask(parent) xor bit(s[v]). The path u–v has character-parity mask mask(u) xor mask(v). So (u,v) is valid iff mask(u)==mask(v) or the masks differ in exactly one bit. Example 1 gives 8 pairs; Example 2 (all 'a') gives all C(5,2)=10 pairs. With n up to 1e5 we need an O(26·n) counting scheme, iterative to avoid recursion-depth crashes.
k: Represent each root-to-node path as a 26-bit parity mask; path(u,v) mask = mask(u) xor mask(v).
Valid pair ⇔ XOR of masks is 0 or a power of two.
Sweep nodes in BFS order, pairing each node against previously seen masks (equal or one-bit-flipped), then insert its mask.

a.i: Compute masks top-down (parent before child) via BFS. Process nodes in BFS order; for node v add cnt[mask(v)] plus Σ_b cnt[mask(v) xor 2^b] from earlier nodes, then increment cnt[mask(v)]. Root contributes mask 0 and pairs with everyone whose mask is 0 or a single bit.
s: Build children lists; BFS from root computing masks.
For each node in BFS order: add existing counts for equal mask and 26 one-bit variants.
Insert the node's mask into the counter.
a.t: O(26 · n) — BFS is O(n); each node checks 27 mask variants in a hash map.
a.sp: O(n) for masks, order, and the counter.

a.i: Instead of an online sweep, count all masks first. Equal-mask pairs contribute Σ C(c,2); one-bit-apart pairs contribute Σ over masks m and bits b of cnt[m]·cnt[m⊕2^b], divided by 2 to undo double counting. Same asymptotics, slightly different bookkeeping.
s: For each mask and bit, add cnt[m]·cnt[m^bit] and halve the total.

w: Use the online sweep (approach 1) — it avoids the halving subtlety. Critical pitfalls: answers exceed 32 bits (use 64-bit), deep trees blow recursion stacks (iterate!), and the root's own mask 0 must participate in counts. Follow-up: characters on nodes instead of edges, or count pairs forming palindromes under at most k odd characters (generalize the one-bit flip to popcount ≤ k with meet-in-the-middle).
